plain: The writer Terence McKenna proposed that human consciousness began when our early ancestors started eating psychedelic mushrooms, an idea known as the "stoned ape" theory. Jeffrey Mishlove, a guest with a doctorate, sums it up on the show: "consciousness itself developed when our primate ancestors discovered these mushrooms." Michels gives his own version on an episode about mushrooms. He says McKenna pictured hunter-gatherers in Africa a couple of million years ago following animal dung to track their prey, and so coming across the mushrooms. The writer Graham Hancock names the source, McKenna's book Food of the Gods, as one of the first books of its kind. On another episode Michels suggests the theory could explain why the brain roughly doubled in size between Homo habilis and Homo sapiens. If it were true, a plant would have played a part in making us who we are.
